message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"5e0b8742d5025f117f81ecd3330f5b501e115e510a35468cd2f4dab5e958237d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:82","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","units":[{"unit_id":"sec04-u01","module_id":"sec04-m01","objective_ids":["sec04-u01"],"title":{"text":"Exam parts and test sets","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The examination has three parts, but each kind of applicant takes a different set.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F07"]},{"text":"Knowing your test set tells you what to prepare and what to schedule.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F08"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Jo holds a Class PD permit and is ready to exchange it for a Class D license.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Exchanging a Class PD permit for a Class D license needs only the vision screening and road skills test.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Jo takes the vision screening and the road skills test, with no new knowledge test.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking every applicant takes all three tests.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R02"]},"correction":{"text":"A Class PD applicant takes only vision and knowledge, a PD exchange needs vision and road, and a renewal needs no test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Original D: all three; PD: two; renewal: none.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A new resident arrives with a current, valid license from another state. Which test does she take?","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"Only the vision screening.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"All three tests apply only if her license is expired, she comes from another country, or she never held a license.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Three exam parts","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vision screening.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]},{"text":"Knowledge test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]},{"text":"Road test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Tennessee driver license examination has three parts: a vision screening, a knowledge test and a road test. Every Driver Service Center gives license tests except the express service centers, and knowledge tests are handled first-come, first-served. Road tests take long enough to administer that they are given only by appointment. This lesson explains which parts each kind of applicant takes, because not every applicant faces all three. Knowing your own test set helps you prepare for the right tests and book only what you need.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Original applicants","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Class D or H: knowledge, road and vision.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R03"]},{"text":"Class PD: vision and knowledge only.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"An original Class D or Class H applicant takes the knowledge test, the road skills test and the vision screening, while a Class PD applicant takes only the vision screening and knowledge test. So a fifteen-year-old applying for a learner permit does not take the road test yet. The road test comes later, when the permit holder moves up. Adding a For-Hire endorsement requires the vision screening and a knowledge test. Each path matches its tests to what the license allows the holder to do on the road. Check which application you are making before you study.","fact_ids":["sec04-F07","sec04-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Exchanges and renewals","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"PD exchange: vision and road test.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},{"text":"Duplicate or renewal: no test at all.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is where people get confused. Exchanging a Class PD permit for a Class D license needs only the vision screening and road skills test, while a duplicate or renewal needs no test at all. So a permit holder moving up does not repeat the knowledge test, and a driver renewing a license does not take any test. Many applicants expect to sit every test at every visit. Match the visit to its test set before you go, so you know whether to prepare for the road test, the knowledge test or nothing. In short, the exchange needs two tests and the renewal needs none.","fact_ids":["sec04-R02","sec04-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"New residents","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid out-of-state license: vision only.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]},{"text":"Expired, foreign or none: all three tests.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"A new resident with a current, valid out-of-state license takes only the vision screening. A new resident whose license is expired, or who comes from another country or never held a license, takes all three tests. So the out-of-state license saves the newcomer from the knowledge and road tests only while it is current and valid. Someone arriving from another country takes the vision screening, knowledge test and road test regardless of what license they held at home. The deciding question is simply whether the out-of-state license is current and valid on the day you apply.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"New resident check","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid out-of-state license: which tests?","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a new resident arrives in Tennessee with a current, valid license from another state. Which test does she take? Work it out before reading on. She takes only the vision screening. All three tests apply when the out-of-state license is expired, when the applicant comes from another country, or when the applicant never held a license. Because her license is current and valid, the knowledge and road tests are not required. She still visits a center that gives tests, which means any center except an express service center.","fact_ids":["sec04-F08","sec04-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Test sets recap","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F07","sec04-R02","sec04-R03","sec04-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Original D or H: three tests.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F07","sec04-R02","sec04-R03","sec04-F08"]},{"text":"PD: two; exchange: two; renewal: none.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F07","sec04-R02","sec04-R03","sec04-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, the examination has three parts, given at every Driver Service Center except express centers, with knowledge tests first-come, first-served and road tests by appointment. An original Class D or H applicant takes all three, a Class PD applicant takes vision and knowledge, a PD exchange takes vision and road, a For-Hire endorsement takes vision and knowledge, and a renewal takes none. New residents with a valid out-of-state license take only the vision screening, while expired, foreign or first-time applicants take all three. Know your set.","fact_ids":["sec04-F01","sec04-F02","sec04-F03","sec04-F07","sec04-R02","sec04-R03","sec04-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec04-u02","module_id":"sec04-m02","objective_ids":["sec04-u02"],"title":{"text":"Vision it.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"The knowledge test is offered in several formats and languages, with strict rules on help.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F13"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ivan's first language is Russian, and he wants help reading the knowledge test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13"]},"reasoning":{"text":"An applicant whose first language is not English may use a translation dictionary free of notes or handwriting, but phones, PDAs and electronic dictionaries are banned and interpreters may not help.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13"]},"result":{"text":"Ivan brings a clean paper translation dictionary and leaves his phone test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"Interpreters may not help with any test, except that the Department supplies a certified sign language interpreter for a deaf applicant's oral test.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Twenty over forty, each eye and both.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Which help may handwriting.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13"]},"rationale":{"text":"Phones, PDAs, electronic dictionaries and interpreters are not allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Seeing and knowing","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"The vision standard.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F11"]},{"text":"The knowledge test and its options.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the vision screening and the knowledge test. The vision screening requires at least twenty over forty vision in each eye alone and in both eyes together, with or without glasses or contact lenses. The knowledge test is multiple choice and built from Sections B and C of the manual. You will learn what happens if you cannot pass the vision screening, how the knowledge test is given and in which languages, what help is allowed, and how some teens can take the written test online with a parent or guardian as proctor.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The vision screening","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty over forty in each eye and both.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"Glasses or contacts allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]},{"text":"Eye statement if you cannot pass.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"The vision standard is the same for each eye alone and for both eyes together: at least twenty over forty, with or without glasses or contact lenses. An applicant who cannot pass the vision screening must have an eye specialist of their choice complete an eye statement for the Department to evaluate. So failing the screening at the center is not the end of the road. The Department reviews the specialist's statement. If you wear glasses or contacts to see clearly, wear them for the screening, since lenses are allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What the knowledge test covers","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Multiple choice, from Sections B and C.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},{"text":"Four areas of roughly equal size.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"The knowledge test is multiple choice, built from Sections B and C of the manual, and is expected to split roughly twenty-five percent each among four areas: traffic signs and signals, safe driving principles, rules of the road, and drugs and alcohol. That tells you how to study. Each of the four areas carries about the same share, so no single area can be skipped. Knowledge tests run on computerized testing machines, with written versions only in very limited cases. Spread your study time evenly across all four areas, from signs and signals to drugs and alcohol, because each one carries a similar share.","fact_ids":["sec04-F11","sec04-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Languages and oral tests","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Spanish, Korean and Japanese versions.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Oral tests by appointment.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Under eighteen: a written statement first.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Centers with computerized testing also offer the knowledge test in Spanish, Korean and Japanese. Oral knowledge tests are offered by appointment at selected centers for applicants who cannot read or have a learning disability, and an applicant under eighteen must first supply a physician's or educational specialist's written statement. When a deaf applicant asks for an oral knowledge test, the Department of Safety supplies a certified sign language interpreter to help administer it. These options are arranged ahead of time, so plan early if you need one.","fact_ids":["sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Help that is not allowed","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Clean translation dictionary: allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Phones, PDAs, electronic dictionaries: banned.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]},{"text":"Interpreters: not allowed.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. An applicant whose first language is not English may use a translation dictionary, but only one free of notes or handwriting. Phones, PDAs and electronic dictionaries are banned, and interpreters may not help with any test. The one exception is the certified sign language interpreter the Department supplies for a deaf applicant's oral test. So a relative offering to translate is not allowed, and neither is a translation app. A plain paper dictionary with no writing in it is the only outside help on this list.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Online test for teens","fact_ids":["sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ages fifteen to seventeen.","fact_ids":["sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},{"text":"Parent or guardian as proctor.","fact_ids":["sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},{"text":"Proctor verified through the PID App.","fact_ids":["sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Teens aged fifteen to seventeen who must take the written test may take it online, supervised by a parent or legal guardian acting as proctor through the Tennessee Proctor Identification App. The PID App lets an eligible proctor obtain a secure personal identification verified against the proctor's own Department of Safety record before supervising an online knowledge test. So the online option still has supervision. The proctor must be the teen's parent or legal guardian, and the app confirms who that proctor is before the test begins.","fact_ids":["sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Allowed help check","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Which help may a non-English speaker use?","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant whose first language is not English asks what help is allowed during the knowledge test. Work it out before reading on. The applicant may use a translation dictionary free of notes or handwriting. Phones, PDAs and electronic dictionaries are banned, and interpreters may not help with any test. The applicant could also check whether a Spanish, Korean or Japanese version of the test is offered at a computerized center, since those versions are available there. Those are the only aids allowed in the room.","fact_ids":["sec04-F13","sec04-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Vision and knowledge recap","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty over forty, each eye and both.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},{"text":"Four equal areas, several formats.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},{"text":"Clean dictionary only; no devices.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, the vision screening requires at least twenty over forty in each eye alone and both together, with or without lenses, and an eye specialist's statement is the path for applicants who cannot pass. The knowledge test is multiple choice from Sections B and C, split roughly equally across four areas, given on computers with Spanish, Korean and Japanese versions, and offered orally by appointment. Only a clean translation dictionary is allowed, with the sign language interpreter exception, and teens may test online with a verified parent or guardian proctor.","fact_ids":["sec04-F09","sec04-F10","sec04-F11","sec04-F12","sec04-F14","sec04-F13","sec04-R05","sec04-F37","sec04-R17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec04-u03","module_id":"sec04-m03","objective_ids":["sec04-u03"],"title":{"text":"Retakes, cheating and conduct","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F06","sec04-F16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Failing and cheating lead to very different waits before the next attempt.","fact_ids":["sec04-R01"]},{"text":"Every retake has costs and paperwork of its own.","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mara failed her knowledge test on Monday morning.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"No test may be repeated on the same day, and after failing a knowledge test you must wait at least one day.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F16"]},"result":{"text":"Mara may try again on Tuesday at the earliest, bringing her original documents and paying the application fee again.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-R04","sec04-F06"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a cheating attempt only costs one more day.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Any cheating means automatic failure and a thirty-day wait, while an ordinary knowledge test failure means a one-day wait.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Fail: wait a day; cheat: wait thirty.","fact_ids":["sec04-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"An applicant is caught with notes written on her hand during the knowledge test. What happens?","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-F15"]},"answer":{"text":"Automatic failure and a thirty-day wait before she may try again.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15"]},"rationale":{"text":"Notes on the body are a form of cheating, and cheating brings the thirty-day wait.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When a test goes wrong","fact_ids":["sec04-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Waiting periods.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05"]},{"text":"Fees and documents.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05"]},{"text":"Cheating and devices.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers what happens after a failed test, what counts as cheating and what conduct is expected in the test room. Start with the simplest rule: no test may be repeated on the same day it was taken. After that, the length of the wait depends on why the attempt ended. You will also learn the fee and document rules for coming back, the forms that cheating can take, and which devices must be switched off during both the written test and the road test. Each rule is short, but the penalties differ a great deal.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"After a failed knowledge test","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wait at least one day.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]},{"text":"Same wait after every failure.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]},{"text":"Never the same day.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"After failing any knowledge test you must wait at least one day before trying again, and the same wait applies after every later failure. Combined with the rule that no test may be repeated on the same day, this means the earliest retake is the next day. There is no limit stated on how many times the wait applies; it simply repeats after each failure. So a failed morning test cannot be retaken that afternoon, and a second failure the next day brings another one-day wait before the third try. So the next day is always the earliest retake.","fact_ids":["sec04-F16","sec04-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Coming back to retest","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pay the application fee again.","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R04"]},{"text":"Bring all original documents again.","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Each time you take and fail a PD, D or H test, you pay the two dollars application fee again. Anyone returning to retake a test must also bring all the required original documents again. So a retake is not just another try at the questions. It is a new visit, with the fee and the original documents required once more. Keep your documents together after a failed attempt, because you will need every one of them when you come back, along with the fee for the new attempt. Treat every retake as a fresh visit with the full paperwork and the fee.","fact_ids":["sec04-F06","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Cheating costs thirty days","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cheating: automatic failure.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]},{"text":"Wait thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]},{"text":"Failure alone: wait one day.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some applicants assume that being caught cheating is treated like any other failure. It is not. Any cheating on a required examination means automatic failure and a thirty-day wait before the test may be attempted again. Waiting periods differ by cause: a failed knowledge test means a one-day wait, while being caught cheating means a thirty-day wait before another attempt. So the difference between an honest failure and a cheating attempt is the difference between trying again tomorrow and waiting a month.","fact_ids":["sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What counts as cheating","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Written notes anywhere.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},{"text":"Talking, including phone use.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},{"text":"Someone else taking the exam.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Forms of cheating include written notes on paper, clothing, the body or devices, talking during the test including phone use, and trying to have someone else take the exam. All cell phones, pagers and text messaging devices must be switched off during both the written test and the road test. So a phone that is on during the test is a problem even if you never look at it, and a quick question to the person next to you counts as talking. Arrive with nothing written on you and your devices switched off. Keep your hands, clothing and devices free of notes.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Cheating check","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Notes on her hand: what happens?","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: during the knowledge test, an examiner finds notes written on an applicant's hand. What happens next? Work it out before reading on. Written notes on the body are one of the forms of cheating. Any cheating on a required examination means automatic failure and a thirty-day wait before the test may be attempted again. That is very different from an ordinary failure, after which the applicant would wait only one day. When she returns, she will also bring her original documents again and pay the application fee again.","fact_ids":["sec04-R06","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec04-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Retakes recap","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F16","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F06","sec04-R04","sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"No same-day retests.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F16","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F06","sec04-R04","sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},{"text":"Fail: one day; cheat: thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F16","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F06","sec04-R04","sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]},{"text":"Fee and documents every retake.","fact_ids":["sec04-F05","sec04-F16","sec04-F15","sec04-R01","sec04-F06","sec04-R04","sec04-R06","sec04-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, no test may be repeated on the same day. After failing a knowledge test, wait at least one day, and the same wait applies after every later failure. Any cheating means automatic failure and a thirty-day wait.
